title: Cap. IV Arg. 8: from the order of execution — whom God saves/destroys in time he decreed from eternity
latin: Arg. 8. Ab ordine exsecutionis sic disputant; Illi et tales quos et quales Deus in tempore salvat et perdit, illos et tales ab aeterno decrevit salvare et perdere: Atqui Deus solos perseverantes in fide, qua tales, in tempore salvat; incredulos, qua tales, perdit: Ergo Deus ab aeterno decrevit solos fideles, qua tales, salvare. Majorem probant ab immutabilitate Dei: Minorem ex perpetua voce Evangelii, quod credentibus vitam pollicetur, incredulis mortem interminatur.
pass_a: Argument 8. From the order of execution they dispute thus; Those and such as God in time saves and destroys, those and such he decreed from eternity to save and to destroy: But God saves in time only those persevering in faith, as such; he destroys unbelievers, as such: Therefore God from eternity decreed to save only the faithful, as such. They prove the Major from the immutability of God: the Minor from the perpetual voice of the Gospel, which promises life to believers, threatens death to unbelievers.
pass_b: Arg. 8. From the order of execution they argue: those and such as God saves and destroys in time, he decreed from eternity to save and destroy. But in time God saves only those who persevere in faith, as such, and destroys unbelievers as such. Therefore from eternity he decreed to save only the faithful as such. They prove the Major from God's immutability; the Minor from the Gospel's standing voice — life promised to believers, death threatened to unbelievers.

lemmas.lemma: salvat et perdit / salvare et perdere
lemmas.gloss: saves and destroys in time vs decree

title: Cap. IV Arg. 8 Sol: conclusion does not force foresight-election; Major mixes Decernere and Servare
latin: Sol. Conclusionem dicimus non directe contradicere sententiae nostrae. Conclusum enim oportuit, Ergo Deus solos fideles, et qua fideles, ex praevisione hujus fidei elegit ad gloriam. Illa autem conclusio, Ergo solos fideles ab aeterno decrevit, qua tales servare, ponit fidem antecedaneam conditionem quoad ipsam externam collationem decretae salutis; quod nos non negamus; non autem quoad ipsum internum decretum Dei ad salutem destinantis; quod probatum oportuit. Ad Majoris ventilationem accedamus. Dico in illa commisceri, et mala fide copulari duo vocabula, quorum unum designat ipsam destinationem ad salutem in mente Divina; alterum perductionem ad salutem in exsecutione externa. Nam verbum Decernere respicit actum voluntatis Divinae aeternum et intrinsecum; verbum Servare respicit effectum extrinsecum et temporalem.
pass_a: Solution. We say that the conclusion does not directly contradict our position. For what ought to have been concluded was, Therefore God elected to glory only the faithful, and as faithful, from foresight of this faith. But that conclusion, Therefore he decreed from eternity to save only the faithful, as such, puts faith as an antecedent condition as to the very external conferring of the decreed salvation; which we do not deny; but not as to the very internal decree of God destinating to salvation; which ought to have been proved. Let us come to the ventilation of the Major. I say that in it two words are mixed and joined in bad faith, of which one designates the very destination to salvation in the Divine mind; the other the leading through to salvation in external execution. For the word to Decree regards the eternal and intrinsic act of the Divine will; the word to Save regards the extrinsic and temporal effect.
pass_b: Sol. The conclusion does not directly contradict us. What they needed was: therefore God elected to glory only the faithful as faithful, from foresight of that faith. Their conclusion — he decreed from eternity to save only the faithful as such — makes faith an antecedent condition for the external conferring of decreed salvation (which we grant), not for God's internal destinating decree (which they needed to prove). On the Major: two words are mixed in bad faith — one names destination to salvation in the divine mind, the other leading to salvation in external execution. Decernere looks to the eternal intrinsic act of will; Servare to the extrinsic temporal effect.

title: Cap. IV Arg. 8 Sol: faith precedes saving Peter, not the eternal decree — head of the error
latin: Jam vero actus Dei internus non habet eas causas, nec requirit eas conditiones praecedaneas, quas habet et praerequirit ipsum externum salutis praedictae effectum. Non servat Petrum Deus nisi fide ejus praecedente; at decernit servare Petrum in gratuito et aeterno voluntatis suae beneplacito, non praecedente hac fide tanquam conditione ad decreti ipsius constitutionem, sed tanquam conditione ad rei decretae opportunam temporalemque effectionem. Caput ergo erroris est, quod qualitas fidei antecedanea, quae cum re decreta conjungi debuit, et eidem in sola exsecutione praeponi, cum actu Dei decernentis conjungatur, et decreto ejus tanquam antecedaneum motivum praeponatur.
pass_a: But now the internal act of God does not have those causes, nor does it require those antecedent conditions, which the very external effect of the aforesaid salvation has and prerequires. God does not save Peter unless with his faith preceding; but he decrees to save Peter in the free and eternal good pleasure of his will, not with this faith preceding as a condition for the constitution of the decree itself, but as a condition for the opportune and temporal effecting of the thing decreed. The head of the error therefore is, that the antecedent quality of faith, which ought to have been joined with the thing decreed, and set before the same in execution alone, is joined with the act of God decreeing, and set before his decree as an antecedent motive.
pass_b: God's internal act does not have the causes or require the antecedent conditions that the external effect of salvation has and prerequires. He does not save Peter unless Peter's faith precedes; yet he decrees to save Peter in the free eternal good pleasure of his will — not with that faith as a condition for constituting the decree, but as a condition for timely temporal effecting of what was decreed. The error's head: the antecedent quality of faith, which should be joined to the thing decreed and set before it only in execution, is joined to God's decreeing act and set before the decree as an antecedent motive.

title: Cap. IV Arg. 8 Sol: king and beggar — robes precede crowning, not the first destination
latin: Exemplo illustrabimus ea quae dicta sunt, et ostendemus quasdam conditiones requiri posse ut previas, quo Petrus servetur, vel in regnum caeleste introducatur, quae non requiruntur ut previae, quo eligatur, sive ad vitam aeternam a Deo destinetur. Ponamus Regem aliquem, conspecto mendico pannis obsito, ulceribus foetido, decernere nihilominus ex mero suo beneplacito hunc talem adoptare, et ad regni coronam evehere; insuper tamen ordinare ut antequam coronetur, regalibus vestimentis induatur, et ab immunditie sua purgetur, neque coronetur nisi prius ita fuerit purgatus et indutus. Quis non videt pulchra haec vestimenta et purgationem decreta et praerequisita fuisse tanquam praecedanea ad actum coronandi, et tamen non fuisse praerequisita tanquam praecedanea motiva ad primam destinationem regni et coronae?
pass_a: By an example we will illustrate the things that have been said, and we will show that certain conditions can be required as previous, in order that Peter may be saved, or introduced into the heavenly kingdom, which are not required as previous in order that he may be elected, or destined by God to eternal life. Let us suppose some King, having seen a beggar clothed in rags, foul with ulcers, nevertheless decrees from his mere good pleasure to adopt this one such, and to raise him to the crown of the kingdom; yet further orders that before he is crowned, he be clothed with royal garments, and purged from his uncleanness, and that he not be crowned unless he has first been thus purged and clothed. Who does not see that these beautiful garments and the purging were decreed and prerequired as antecedent to the act of crowning, and yet were not prerequired as antecedent motives to the first destination of the kingdom and crown?
pass_b: An example: some conditions can be required beforehand so that Peter is saved or brought into the heavenly kingdom, without being required beforehand so that he is elected or destined by God to eternal life. Suppose a king sees a beggar in rags, foul with ulcers, yet from mere good pleasure decrees to adopt him and raise him to the kingdom's crown — and also orders that before crowning he be clothed in royal garments and purged of uncleanness, and not crowned until thus purged and clothed. Who does not see those fair garments and the purging were decreed and prerequired as antecedent to crowning, yet not as antecedent motives for the first destination of kingdom and crown?

title: Cap. IV Arg. 8 Sol: Remonstrant syllogism on foresight-robes is mere trifles; apply to elect
latin: Fiat ergo syllogismus ad exemplar propositum a Remonstrantibus, et vanitas ejus illico patebit: Ille et talis quem et qualem hic Rex in tempore coronavit, illum et talem ab initio coronare decrevit: Sed pulchre vestitum et a squalore suo purgatum, qua talem, in tempore coronat: Ergo ab initio decrevit pulchre vestitum, qua talem, hoc est, ex praevisa conditione pulchrorum vestimentorum, adoptare et coronare. Nugae merae. Non enim prima voluntas adoptandi et coronandi originem cepit ab antecedanea consideratione, aut praevisa conditione pulchrorum vestimentorum; sed ipsa actio coronandi requirebat haec vestimenta et hanc purgationem antecedaneam, idque ex decreto Regis externam rei exsecutionem ordinante. Accommodemus haec praesenti instituto. Deus Petrum, Paulum, vel quemlibet electum in massa veteris Adami corruptum et peccato tabidum, ex beneplacito mero voluntatis suae vult adoptare, et aeterna vita donare: Sed decernit etiam, et in Evangelio hoc decretum promulgat, velle se ut fide prius purificetur, et a sordibus peccatorum mundetur, quam in possessionem regni introducatur.
pass_a: Let the syllogism therefore be made after the pattern proposed by the Remonstrants, and its vanity will at once be plain: He and such as this King crowned in time, him and such he decreed from the beginning to crown: But he crowns in time one beautifully clothed and purged from his squalor, as such: Therefore from the beginning he decreed to adopt and crown one beautifully clothed, as such, that is, from the foresight condition of beautiful garments. Mere trifles. For the first will of adopting and crowning did not take its origin from an antecedent consideration, or from the foresight condition of beautiful garments; but the very act of crowning required these garments and this antecedent purging, and that from the King's decree ordering the external execution of the thing. Let us accommodate these things to the present design. God wills to adopt Peter, Paul, or any elect corrupted in the mass of old Adam and wasting with sin, from the mere good pleasure of his will, and to gift eternal life: But he also decrees, and promulgates this decree in the Gospel, that he wills that he first be purified by faith, and cleansed from the filth of sins, before he is introduced into possession of the kingdom.
pass_b: Run the Remonstrants' pattern and its vanity shows at once: whom and as such this king crowned in time, he decreed from the start to crown as such; but in time he crowns one beautifully clothed and purged of squalor as such; therefore from the start he decreed to adopt and crown one beautifully clothed as such — i.e. from foresight of fair garments. Mere trifles. The first will to adopt and crown did not spring from foresight of garments; crowning itself required those garments and that prior purging, by the king's decree ordering external execution. Apply it: God from mere good pleasure wills to adopt Peter, Paul, or any elect corrupt in old Adam's mass and wasting in sin, and gift eternal life — yet also decrees, and publishes in the Gospel, that he wills him first purified by faith and cleansed from sin's filth before entering the kingdom.

lemmas.gloss: first purified by faith before kingdom

title: Cap. IV Arg. 8 Sol close: faith antecedent to execution not to eternal will; Minor — temporal prereqs
latin: Erit jam consideratio Petri ut fidelis et a peccatis purgati antecedanea ad exsecutionem rei volitae; salutis scilicet acquisitionem, idque ex decreto Dei: sed non erit antecedanea ad ipsam voluntatem Dei de Petro servando, qui utrumque decrevit, et servare Petrum, et priusquam servetur fide illum donare. Neque immutabilitatem Divinae naturae labefactat quod ponitur, decernere aliquid tanquam praecedaneum ad rei decretae actualem productionem, quod non est praecedaneum ad internam Dei de re producenda volitionem. Ratio manifesta est; Quia Effectum salutis in subjecto praedestinato et decretum salutis dandae in voluntate praedestinantis sunt res diversae, nec easdem causas aut conditiones previas requirunt. De Minore nil aliud dico, quam multa praerequiri ut quis in tempore salvatur, quae non erant praerequisita ut ab aeterno ad salutem eligeretur, sed potius media praedestinato postmodum conferenda ut ad salutem perduceretur.
pass_a: The consideration of Peter as faithful and purged from sins will now be antecedent to the execution of the thing willed; namely the acquisition of salvation, and that from the decree of God: but it will not be antecedent to the very will of God concerning saving Peter, who decreed both, both to save Peter, and before he is saved to gift him with faith. Nor does it weaken the immutability of the Divine nature that it is put that something is decreed as antecedent to the actual production of the thing decreed, which is not antecedent to the internal volition of God concerning the thing to be produced. The reason is plain; Because the Effect of salvation in the predestinated subject and the decree of salvation to be given in the will of the predestinating One are diverse things, and do not require the same causes or previous conditions. Concerning the Minor I say nothing else, than that many things are prerequired in order that someone be saved in time, which were not prerequired in order that he be elected from eternity to salvation, but rather means afterward to be conferred on the predestinated in order that he be led through to salvation.
pass_b: Peter as faithful and purged of sins is antecedent to executing what was willed — acquiring salvation, by God's decree — but not antecedent to God's will to save Peter, who decreed both: to save Peter, and to gift him faith before he is saved. Nor does that unsettle divine immutability: something may be decreed as antecedent to actually producing what was decreed without being antecedent to God's internal volition about producing it. Reason: the effect of salvation in the predestinated subject and the decree to give salvation in the predestinating will are diverse things and do not require the same prior causes or conditions. On the Minor: many things are prerequired for someone to be saved in time that were not prerequired for eternal election to salvation — rather means later conferred on the predestinated so he is led through to salvation.
